findings: "localhost:59068" also admitted 192.168.1.70:59068 — this Mac's own en0 address, which SBPL/the kernel treat as local. Not a remote host; a true other-host case needs a second machine.
port-scoped refusals all hold under deny-default: other port, UDP, listen, file read, home listing, exec, unix-socket connect (EPERM).

SBPL refuses a literal IP host in (remote tcp "<ip>:<port>"): only localhost or * compile. A real LAN peer can be pinned by PORT only in the profile; the host must be enforced elsewhere (the child dialing only root-signed addresses, plus a kernel-side peer check / pf) — §15.5 `link` text needs that caveat.
with "*:59068" the child reached 192.168.1.70:59068 — a port-only rule admits any host on that port.
